question.problem:
The function $g(x)$ is given by

$$
g(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x-b}-\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b}}, & x\ne 0, \\ 10, & x=0.\end{aligned}
$$

For what value of $b$ is the function continuous at $x=0?$

$b=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To calculate the limit, we multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}g(x) & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x}{\sqrt{x-b}-\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}(\frac{x}{\sqrt{x-b}-\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{x-b}+\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b}}{\sqrt{x-b}+\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b}}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x-b}+\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b})}{(\sqrt{x-b})^{2}-(\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b})^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x-b}+\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b})}{x-2{x}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{x(\sqrt{x-b}+\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b})}{x(1-2x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\cancel{x}(\sqrt{x-b}+\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b})}{\cancel{x}(1-2x)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{x-b}+\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-b}}{1-2x} \\  & =2\sqrt{-b}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order for $g(x)$ to be continuous at $x=0,$ we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}g(x) & =g(0) \\ 2\sqrt{-b} & =10 \\ \sqrt{-b} & =5 \\ -b & =25 \\ b & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting $b=-25$ removes the point discontinuity.
